evals.name: empty-cluster-must-not-score
evals.prompt:
Run a Well-Architected review of EKS cluster `bare-sandbox` in eu-west-1 in `auto` mode. Activate the eks-well-architected-review skill and run its workflow through the Step 7 reducer, then report the reducer's verdict.

Mock collected cluster data:
- `cluster.json`: name bare-sandbox, ACTIVE, version 1.31, eu-west-1, VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, `computeConfig.enabled` absent, endpointPublicAccess true, endpointPrivateAccess false, secrets encryption not configured, control-plane logging: no log types enabled
- `nodes.json`: `{"items": []}`: zero nodes
- `pods.json`: `{"items": []}`: zero pods in every namespace, including kube-system
- `fargate.json`: `{"fargateProfileNames": []}`
- `deployments.json`, `sg.json`, and every other collection: empty item lists

Produce the review output. Do NOT fabricate findings: report only from the mock data above.
evals.expected_output: A report whose headline is the reducer's NOT VIABLE verdict (the `technical_overall` string, reported verbatim) that emits NO numeric technical overall. Pillar scores may still appear, but each is labelled declared configuration only and marked not comparable to a running cluster's. It reports the control-plane facts (version 1.31, public endpoint, no secrets encryption, no control-plane logging), and states how many questions were applicable.
expectations: The output declares the cluster NOT VIABLE (no data plane) because it has no Linux node: the verdict keys on the node count alone, not on pods.
The response does not re-derive the viability verdict itself.
No numeric technical overall is emitted: an empty cluster must never be rated Excellent, Good, Fair, Needs Improvement, or Poor overall.
Any pillar score that is shown is labelled declared configuration only.
Any pillar score that is shown is marked not comparable to a running cluster's.
Control-plane facts are still reported: Kubernetes version 1.31.
Control-plane facts are still reported: public API endpoint enabled with private disabled.
Control-plane facts are still reported: secrets encryption not configured.
Control-plane facts are still reported: no control-plane log types enabled.
The output states how many questions were applicable rather than silently omitting the count.
The skill does not invent node, pod, workload, or cost findings that the empty collections cannot support.

knowledge_assertions.context: Must report the NOT VIABLE verdict the reducer emits for a cluster with no data plane

evals.name: standard-cluster-deterministic-score
evals.prompt:
Run a Well-Architected review of EKS cluster `prod-payments` in us-east-1 in `auto` mode. Activate the eks-well-architected-review skill and run the full workflow: prerequisites, cluster identification, collection into `$WORK`, mode detection, viability precondition, all five pillar scorer blocks, the Step 7 reducer, and the Step 8 HTML render.

Mock collected cluster data:
- `cluster.json`: name prod-payments, ACTIVE, version 1.30, us-east-1, `computeConfig.enabled` absent (not Auto Mode), endpointPublicAccess false, endpointPrivateAccess true, secrets encryption configured with a KMS key, control-plane logging: api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler all enabled, authenticationMode API_AND_CONFIG_MAP
- `nodes.json`: 9 nodes, all `eks.amazonaws.com/compute-type` unset (EC2), instance types m6i.2xlarge (6) and m7g.2xlarge (3), spread across 3 AZs
- `pods.json`: 84 pods total: 71 in workload namespaces (payments, ledger, web), 13 in kube-system
- `deployments.json`: 22 workload Deployments; 19 define both resource requests and limits, 3 define neither; 14 have a PodDisruptionBudget, 8 do not
- `fargate.json`: `{"fargateProfileNames": []}`
- `sg.json`: no security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 on any port
- Addons: vpc-cni, coredns, kube-proxy, aws-ebs-csi-driver all present and on supported versions; no metrics-server
- HPAs: 11 of 22 Deployments have an HPA; no Cluster Autoscaler and no Karpenter installed
- Storage: 6 PVs, all gp3, all encrypted
- Spot adoption: 0%, every node is On-Demand. Graviton: 3 of 9 nodes are m7g

Produce the review output plus the rendered HTML report. Do NOT fabricate findings: report only from the mock data above.
evals.expected_output: A scored review with a numeric technical overall and a numeric score plus a coverage figure (the reducer's coverage percentage, or the applicable/total count) for each of the five pillars, derived from the Step 7 reducer rather than from hand arithmetic. Security scores well (private endpoint, secrets encryption, full control-plane logging, no 0.0.0.0/0 rules). Reliability is dragged down by the 8 Deployments with no PDB and the absent cluster autoscaler. The Cost pillar is explicitly labelled cost hygiene, with Spot (0%) and Graviton (3 of 9) named as narrative opportunities that are NOT inside that score. A self-contained HTML report is written and its path is reported.
expectations: A numeric technical overall score is emitted.
A numeric score is emitted for each of the five pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization).
A coverage figure (the reducer's coverage percentage, or the applicable/total count) is emitted for each of the five pillars.
The response does not recompute or adjust any pillar number by hand.
The Security pillar's passing findings cite the private-only API endpoint.
The Security pillar's passing findings cite KMS secrets encryption.
The Security pillar's passing findings cite all five control-plane log types.
The Security pillar's passing findings cite the absence of any 0.0.0.0/0 security group rule.
Reliability findings cite the 8 Deployments lacking a PodDisruptionBudget.
Reliability findings cite the absence of Cluster Autoscaler.
Reliability findings cite the absence of Karpenter.
The 3 Deployments with neither requests nor limits are cited under Performance Efficiency or Reliability.
The Cost Optimization score is labelled as cost hygiene.
The response states that Spot (0% adoption), Graviton (3 of 9 nodes), and Extended Support are narrative opportunities that are NOT folded into the Cost Optimization score.
Governance questions are reported as Not Assessed.
Governance questions are never guessed or scored `none`.
Governance questions are not folded into the technical overall.
A self-contained HTML report is produced via `assets/render-report.py`; the HTML is not hand-written.
The filesystem path of the HTML report is stated.

evals.name: fargate-only-na-and-coverage-gate
evals.prompt:
Run a Well-Architected review of EKS cluster `serverless-tenant` in ap-southeast-1 in `auto` mode using the eks-well-architected-review skill. Pay particular attention to Step 3 mode detection and the Step 7 coverage gate.

Mock collected cluster data:
- `cluster.json`: name serverless-tenant, ACTIVE, version 1.29, ap-southeast-1, `computeConfig.enabled` absent, endpointPublicAccess true, endpointPrivateAccess true, secrets encryption not configured, control-plane logging: audit only
- `fargate.json`: `{"fargateProfileNames": ["default", "apps"]}`
- `nodes.json`: 4 nodes, every one labelled `eks.amazonaws.com/compute-type: fargate`, so EC2_NODES is 0
- `pods.json`: 17 pods: 12 in the `apps` namespace, 5 in kube-system
- `deployments.json`: 5 workload Deployments, all with requests and limits, none with a PodDisruptionBudget
- No DaemonSets. No node groups. No Karpenter. No EBS volumes and no PVs.

Produce the review output. Do NOT fabricate findings: report only from the mock data above.
evals.expected_output: A review that detects Fargate-only mode (FARGATE_PROFILES 2, EC2_NODES 0) and marks EC2, DaemonSet, and node-hardening questions `na` rather than `none`. Any pillar whose applicable count falls below 50% of its measured questions reports INSUFFICIENT instead of a number, and the technical overall is WITHHELD if fewer than 4 pillars are numeric. Findings still flag the public API endpoint, missing secrets encryption, audit-only control-plane logging, and the absent PDBs.
expectations: The response detects Fargate-only mode by reporting FARGATE_PROFILES as 2 and EC2_NODES as 0.
The response names the mode explicitly as Fargate-only rather than Standard or Auto.
EC2-specific, DaemonSet, and node-hardening questions are marked `na` and excluded from scoring: they are NOT scored `none`, which would wrongly penalise a cluster that has no EC2 nodes to harden.
The coverage gate is applied: any pillar whose applicable questions fall below 50% of its measured questions is reported as INSUFFICIENT with no number.
The coverage gate is applied: the technical overall is WITHHELD if fewer than 4 pillars are numeric.
A coverage figure (the reducer's coverage percentage, or the applicable/total count) is reported per pillar so a reader can see which pillars were gated and why.
Findings still flag this genuinely observable weakness: public API endpoint enabled.
Findings still flag this genuinely observable weakness: secrets encryption not configured.
Findings still flag this genuinely observable weakness: control-plane logging limited to audit only.
Findings still flag this genuinely observable weakness: 5 Deployments with no PodDisruptionBudget.
